significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—“reversal rate tracks a language's cue-hierarchy distance from the dominant language rather than its resource level”—together with a form-(ii) mechanism in which a shared role-binding representation is causally controlled by dominant-language cue arbitration; this fixes expected error ordering across languages and explains why reliable case or voice morphology can lose to word order. It therefore establishes both a substantial behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, sharper than the representational sharing documented in Chi et al.'s “Finding Universal Grammatical Relations in Multilingual BERT” and Papadimitriou et al.'s “Deep Subjecthood,” because the licensed conclusion predicts behavior from independently measurable cue hierarchy and separates abstract roles from their language-specific assignment. The negative branch is also informative if reversals instead track resource or remain at canonical-control levels, since that rules out dominant-language cue-hierarchy import as the explanation, although failure to localize or steer the role representation would reject only the bundled mechanistic component. True and false outcomes are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: deleting the specific cue-distance law and role-binding/arbitration mechanism leaves only generic cross-language representation research, which would not merit this rating.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two named handles: the “per-language cue-hierarchy index” as a predictor of reversal risk and the “role direction” as an intervention that can “repair or induce reversals.” The cue-hierarchy handle is ex ante because auditors could prioritize case- and voice-dominant languages before deployment, while the steering handle acts after a vulnerable model has been identified; likely downstream users include “multilingual eval builders, model auditors, [and] translation researchers,” not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive distance–reversal relation still predicts the ordering of language failures across the asserted class of multilingual generative models, whereas the particular steering direction itself must be rediscovered and does not transfer numerically. The topic-substitution check supports an above-median score: the generic topic offers no comparable forecasting quantity, auditing rule, or intervention, though the claim stops short of asserting an architecture-invariant quantitative function that would justify reach of 9–10.
